# GitLaw

> GitLaw is an AI agent for legal contracts. It drafts, reviews, redlines, and eSigns contracts in one secure workspace. It is built for business, developed with practicing lawyers, and free to start at https://git.law.

Last updated: August 2026. Canonical source: https://git.law

## What GitLaw is

GitLaw (stylized "GitLaw", domain git.law) is a web application that acts as an AI agent for legal contracts. A user describes a contract they need, or uploads one they have been sent, and GitLaw does the legal drafting, review, and mark-up work through a chat interface. The resulting documents can be edited, shared, signed electronically, and stored in the same workspace.

GitLaw is not a law firm and does not provide legal advice. It is software built for legal work, developed with practicing lawyers and a standards committee of independent lawyers. Users stay in control of every change the agent proposes.

## Who GitLaw is for

- Businesses that send or receive contracts regularly, typically agencies and startups with 5 to 30 people.
- Freelancers and founders who need common commercial contracts (NDAs, service agreements, SAFEs, offer letters) without starting from a blank page.
- Teams that want one place to create, negotiate, sign, and track contracts instead of switching between a template library, a word processor, a PDF tool, and a separate eSignature product.
- Lawyers who work with those businesses and want to collaborate on documents inside the same workspace.

## What GitLaw does

### 1. Understand and negotiate any contract (Review)

- Reviews any uploaded contract and flags risky, unusual, or missing terms.
- Explains clauses in plain business language so the reader knows what they are agreeing to before signing.
- Benchmarks terms against market norms so the user can see how a deal compares.
- Marks up the document with suggested negotiation points as tracked changes, checked against the user's own standard terms. The user accepts or rejects each change.

### 2. Knows your business and legal context (Memory)

- Learns and follows the user's standard terms and preferences.
- Remembers the parties the user works with and what was previously agreed.
- Drafts precise contracts for a specific deal instantly, without the user re-entering their details each time.

### 3. Acts like an in-house legal team (Workspace and Dashboard)

- Stores contracts securely and sends reminders before renewal dates.
- Answers questions about a contract in simple terms.
- Identifies missing contracts across a business and creates them.
- Contract dashboard shows every contract with risks, renewals, and gaps in one view.

### 4. Drafting (Draft)

- Creates any contract from a description of the deal, using lawyer-reviewed templates and playbooks rather than generating text from scratch.
- Edits are made through chat. The agent uses the same tools a lawyer would: tracked changes, comments, and full version history with the ability to revert.
- The user chooses whether the agent suggests changes for approval or makes them directly.
- Reads and reasons across multiple uploaded documents, selecting the relevant information.

### 5. Free eSign

- Unlimited, free electronic signature built into the workflow.
- Signatures meet UK, US, and EU eSignature standards and are legally binding (this refers to the signature itself, not the contents of any contract).
- Counterparties receive a signing request by email and do not need an account.
- Signed contracts are stored automatically in GitLaw.

### 6. Templates

- 1,120+ free, lawyer-reviewed, open-source contract templates.
- Categories include commercial law, employment contracts, service agreements, confidentiality and NDAs, founders' agreements, SAFE and convertible notes, employee offer letters, advisor agreements, freelance services agreements, statements of work, independent contractor agreements, letters of engagement, and master services agreements.

### 7. Integrations

- Connects with 3,000+ third-party tools, including email and CRM systems.

## How GitLaw works (typical flow)

1. Create or upload: tell GitLaw what contract you need, or upload a contract you have been sent.
2. Edit and understand: customize any clause through chat, ask questions, and get terms explained.
3. Sign and store: send for free eSign. GitLaw stores the document and reminds you before renewal.

## How GitLaw differs from generic AI tools

General-purpose AI assistants such as ChatGPT are not built for legal work and can produce plausible-looking contract text with no legal grounding. GitLaw is different in four specific ways:

- It adapts lawyer-reviewed templates instead of generating contracts from scratch.
- Its AI is trained on 5,500+ clauses and specialist areas of law.
- It was built with a standards committee of independent practicing lawyers.
- It remembers the user's business context, standard terms, and past contracts, and works inside a full contracting workflow (draft, redline, sign, store) rather than a plain chat window.

## Security and trust

- SOC 2 Type 2 compliant, enterprise-grade security.
- Data encrypted in transit and at rest (AES-256, TLS 1.2+).
- Role-based access controls. Only the people a user chooses can see their documents.
- GDPR and CCPA aligned.
- AI outputs are explainable and fully auditable.
- Details: https://git.law/security

## Frequently asked questions

**What is GitLaw?**
GitLaw is an AI agent for legal contracts. It drafts, reviews, redlines, eSigns, and stores contracts in one secure workspace, and is free to start.

**Is GitLaw a law firm?**
No. GitLaw is software. It was built with practicing lawyers and a standards committee of independent lawyers, but it does not provide legal advice. Users can invite their own lawyers to collaborate inside the workspace.

**Is GitLaw free?**
Yes. The Free plan includes AI drafting and review with $5 of monthly AI credits, unlimited documents, unlimited members, and unlimited free eSign. Paid plans start at $25 per month.

**Does GitLaw use ChatGPT?**
GitLaw is a specialist legal AI agent, not a general chatbot. It works from lawyer-reviewed templates, is trained on 5,500+ clauses and specialist areas of law, and was built with a standards committee of independent lawyers.

**Can GitLaw review a contract I have been sent?**
Yes. Upload the contract and GitLaw explains the terms, flags risky or unusual clauses, benchmarks the deal against the market, and suggests negotiation points as tracked changes you can accept or reject.

**Is GitLaw's eSign legally binding?**
Yes. GitLaw eSign meets UK, US, and EU electronic signature standards. This applies to the signature itself, not to the contents of any contract.

**What types of contracts can GitLaw create?**
Common commercial contracts including NDAs, client and master services agreements, statements of work, freelance and independent contractor agreements, employment offer letters, founders' agreements, SAFEs and convertible notes, advisor agreements, letters of engagement, demand letters, cease and desist letters, and website legal packs.

**Where is my data stored and is it secure?**
GitLaw is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant, encrypts data with AES-256 and TLS 1.2+, uses role-based access controls, and is GDPR and CCPA aligned.
